definitions.explanation: Physically heavy or weighty. A colloquial variant of 重い that emphasizes the subjective sensation of heaviness.

examples.japanese: この{荷物|にもつ}、{重|おも}たい。
{買|か}い{物|もの}の{袋|ふくろ}が{重|おも}たくて{腕|うで}が{痛|いた}い。
examples.english: The shopping bags are so heavy that my arms hurt.

examples.japanese: {食|た}べ{過|す}ぎて{胃|い}が{重|おも}たく{感|かん}じる。
examples.english: I ate too much and my stomach feels heavy.

notes:
A colloquial form of {重|おも}い. While {重|おも}い is neutral and used in both spoken and written contexts, {重|おも}たい is primarily spoken and conveys a stronger sense of personal, physical sensation of heaviness.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {荷物|にもつ}が{重|おも}たい (the luggage is heavy)
- {足|あし}が{重|おも}たい (one's legs feel heavy)
- {頭|あたま}が{重|おも}たい (one's head feels heavy)

USAGE NOTE:
{重|おも}たい sounds more casual and subjective than {重|おも}い. Use {重|おも}い in writing, measurements, and objective descriptions. Use {重|おも}たい when expressing how something feels to you personally.
